description: This topic covers the meaning and branches of horticulture, its importance, the establishment and management of vegetable gardens and nurseries, propagation methods, production of common vegetables and fruits, harvesting and handling of produce, and the use of greenhouses and irrigation in Tanzania.

mcq.questionText: What is the meaning of horticulture?

options.text: The growing of fruits, vegetables and ornamental plants
The keeping of farm animals for meat and milk
The growing of cereal crops on a large scale
The management of forests for timber production

mcq.explanation: Horticulture is the branch of agriculture dealing with the intensive cultivation of fruits, vegetables, flowers and other ornamental plants.

mcq.questionText: The branch of horticulture concerned with the growing of vegetables is called:
mcq.explanation: Olericulture is the branch of horticulture that deals with the production of vegetables such as tomatoes, cabbages and amaranth.

mcq.questionText: Which branch of horticulture deals with the growing of fruits?
mcq.explanation: Pomology, also called fruit growing, is the branch of horticulture concerned with the production of fruits like mangoes, oranges and bananas.
Floriculture is the branch of horticulture that deals with the growing of flowers and ornamental plants used for decoration and beauty.

mcq.questionText: Which of the following is an importance of horticulture to a family?

options.text: It supplies vitamins and minerals in the diet
It reduces the need for clean water

mcq.explanation: Fruits and vegetables from horticulture supply vitamins and minerals, improving family nutrition and health.

mcq.questionText: A nursery in horticulture is best defined as:

options.text: A store for keeping harvested produce
A protected area where young seedlings are raised before transplanting
A place where animals are kept young
A field where mature crops are left to dry

mcq.explanation: A nursery is a small, well-managed and protected area where seeds are sown and seedlings are raised until they are strong enough to be transplanted.

mcq.questionText: Pricking out in nursery management refers to:

options.text: Transferring crowded seedlings to give them wider spacing

mcq.explanation: Pricking out is the careful moving of crowded young seedlings into wider spacing or into pots so they have enough room to grow strong.

mcq.questionText: Which propagation method involves joining a scion onto a rootstock so that they grow as one plant?
mcq.explanation: Grafting joins a scion (upper shoot) to a rootstock so that the two unite and grow as a single plant, commonly used for fruit trees like mangoes and oranges.

mcq.questionText: Mulching a vegetable garden mainly helps to:

options.text: Conserve soil moisture and control weeds
Make the soil more acidic permanently

mcq.explanation: Mulch covers the soil, reduces water loss through evaporation, suppresses weeds and helps keep the soil cool and moist.

mcq.questionText: Which of the following vegetables is a leafy vegetable commonly grown in Tanzania?
mcq.explanation: Amaranth (mchicha) is a popular leafy vegetable in Tanzania, grown for its tender leaves which are rich in vitamins and minerals.

mcq.questionText: When raising a tomato nursery, the seedbed should be sited where there is:

options.text: Waterlogged, shaded ground far from water
Fertile, well-drained soil near a water source
Rocky soil with no access to water
Land that has just grown tomatoes the previous season

mcq.explanation: A good nursery site has fertile, well-drained soil, is close to a reliable water source and is protected, ensuring healthy seedling growth.

mcq.questionText: A greenhouse is used in horticulture mainly to:

options.text: Control the growing environment such as temperature and humidity
Increase wind speed over the crop
Replace the need for any watering
Reduce crop yields per unit area

mcq.explanation: A greenhouse encloses crops to control temperature, humidity and protect them from pests and harsh weather, allowing higher quality and out-of-season production.

mcq.questionText: Which irrigation method delivers water directly and slowly to the base of each plant, saving water?
mcq.explanation: Drip irrigation applies water slowly through pipes and emitters to the root zone of each plant, using water efficiently and reducing wastage.

mcq.questionText: Which of the following fruits is propagated mainly by suckers in Tanzania?
mcq.explanation: Bananas are propagated vegetatively using suckers (young shoots from the parent plant) rather than seeds.

mcq.questionText: Harvesting horticultural produce at the correct stage of maturity is important because it:

options.text: Lowers the market value of the produce
Ensures good quality and longer shelf life

mcq.explanation: Harvesting at the right maturity stage gives produce of good quality, better taste and longer shelf life, fetching a higher market price.

fib.questionText: The branch of horticulture that deals with the growing of vegetables is called _____.
fib.explanation: Olericulture is vegetable production, one of the three main branches of horticulture.

fib.questionText: The branch of horticulture concerned with growing fruits is known as _____.
fib.explanation: Pomology, or fruit growing, deals with the production of fruits such as mangoes and oranges.

fib.questionText: The growing of flowers and ornamental plants is called _____.
fib.explanation: Floriculture is the branch of horticulture dealing with flowers and ornamental plants.

fib.questionText: A protected area where seeds are sown and seedlings are raised before transplanting is called a _____.
fib.explanation: Seedlings are first raised in a nursery and later transplanted to the main garden.

fib.questionText: Covering the soil surface with dry grass or other materials to conserve moisture is called _____.
fib.explanation: Mulching conserves soil moisture, controls weeds and keeps the soil cool.

fib.questionText: Moving young crowded seedlings into wider spacing in the nursery is known as _____.
fib.explanation: Pricking out gives seedlings more room to develop strong roots and shoots.

fib.questionText: The method of propagation in which a stem is bent and partly buried to form roots while still attached to the parent plant is called _____.
fib.explanation: In layering, a shoot is induced to root while still attached to the mother plant before being separated.

fib.questionText: The irrigation method that supplies water slowly to the root zone of each plant through pipes and emitters is called _____ irrigation.
fib.explanation: Drip irrigation is water-efficient and ideal for vegetable and fruit production.

fib.questionText: A structure with transparent walls used to control the growing environment of crops is called a _____.
fib.explanation: A greenhouse controls temperature and humidity and protects crops from pests and harsh weather.

fib.questionText: Bananas are commonly propagated using young shoots from the parent plant called _____.
fib.explanation: Banana plants are propagated vegetatively by separating and planting suckers.

tf.questionText: Horticulture includes the growing of fruits, vegetables and ornamental plants.
tf.explanation: These three groups make up the main branches of horticulture: pomology, olericulture and floriculture.

tf.questionText: Olericulture is the branch of horticulture that deals with the growing of fruit trees.
tf.explanation: Olericulture deals with vegetables; fruit growing is called pomology.

tf.questionText: Fruits and vegetables are important sources of vitamins and minerals in the human diet.
tf.explanation: Horticultural produce improves family nutrition by supplying essential vitamins and minerals.

tf.questionText: Horticulture can provide income, employment and export earnings in Tanzania.
tf.explanation: Selling fruits, vegetables and flowers earns income, creates jobs and brings foreign exchange through exports.

tf.questionText: A nursery site should be located far from any water source to avoid flooding.
tf.explanation: A nursery should be near a reliable water source so seedlings can be watered easily, while still being well-drained.

tf.questionText: Mulching helps to reduce water loss from the soil through evaporation.
tf.explanation: Mulch covers the soil and reduces evaporation, conserving moisture for the crop.

tf.questionText: Grafting and budding are methods of vegetative propagation used in fruit growing.
tf.explanation: Grafting and budding join plant parts to a rootstock and are widely used to propagate fruit trees like citrus and mango.

tf.questionText: Tomatoes are usually raised first in a nursery and then transplanted to the field.
tf.explanation: Tomato seeds are sown in a nursery and the seedlings are transplanted when strong enough.

tf.questionText: Drip irrigation uses more water than flood irrigation to grow vegetables.
tf.explanation: Drip irrigation is more water-efficient than flood irrigation because it delivers water directly to the roots.

tf.questionText: Harvesting horticultural produce too early or too late lowers its quality and market value.
tf.explanation: Produce must be harvested at the correct maturity stage to ensure good quality, taste and shelf life.

summary.correctAnswer: Horticulture is the intensive cultivation of fruits, vegetables, flowers and other ornamental plants.
summary.explanation: It is a specialised branch of agriculture focused on garden crops grown intensively.

summary.questionText: Name the three main branches of horticulture.
summary.correctAnswer: Olericulture (vegetables), pomology (fruits) and floriculture (flowers and ornamentals).
summary.explanation: These branches are classified according to the type of horticultural crop grown.

summary.correctAnswer: It improves nutrition, provides income, creates employment and earns foreign exchange through export.
summary.explanation: Horticulture supports health, the economy and livelihoods.

summary.questionText: List the main steps in establishing a vegetable nursery.
summary.correctAnswer: Select a good site, prepare the seedbed, sow seeds, water, mulch, prick out and care for seedlings before transplanting.
summary.explanation: These steps ensure healthy seedlings ready for the main garden.

summary.questionText: Mention four methods of propagation used in horticulture.
summary.correctAnswer: Seeds, cuttings, budding, grafting and layering.
summary.explanation: Horticultural crops are propagated by seed or by vegetative methods.

summary.questionText: Give two examples of vegetables and two examples of fruits grown in Tanzania.
summary.correctAnswer: Vegetables: tomatoes and amaranth (mchicha); fruits: mangoes and bananas.
summary.explanation: Other examples include cabbages, onions, oranges and pawpaw.

summary.questionText: Explain the importance of mulching in a vegetable garden.
summary.correctAnswer: Mulching conserves soil moisture, controls weeds, keeps the soil cool and protects it from erosion.
summary.explanation: Mulch improves growing conditions and reduces the need for frequent watering.

summary.questionText: What is the role of a greenhouse in horticulture?
summary.correctAnswer: A greenhouse controls temperature and humidity, protects crops from pests and harsh weather, and allows high-quality and out-of-season production.
summary.explanation: It creates a favourable, controlled environment for crop growth.

summary.questionText: Why is drip irrigation suitable for horticulture in dry areas?
summary.correctAnswer: It delivers water slowly to the root zone, saving water and reducing wastage and weed growth.
summary.explanation: Drip irrigation is efficient and ideal where water is scarce.

summary.questionText: Why should horticultural produce be harvested at the correct stage of maturity?
summary.correctAnswer: To ensure good quality, better taste, longer shelf life and a higher market price.
summary.explanation: Proper timing of harvest reduces losses and increases value.

hoq.questionText: A farmer in Iringa grafts an improved mango scion onto a local mango rootstock instead of growing the improved variety from seed. Why is grafting the better choice here?

options.text: Grafting keeps the desired qualities of the improved variety and gives a hardy root system that bears fruit sooner
Grafting produces seeds faster than flowering
Seedling mangoes always die within one year
Grafting removes the need for any watering of the tree

hoq.explanation: Mango seedlings do not breed true to type and take long to fruit. Grafting combines the improved scion's quality with a hardy local rootstock, ensuring the desired variety and earlier, reliable fruiting.

hoq.questionText: A horticulturist in Arusha wants to grow high-quality tomatoes for export during the rainy season when field tomatoes suffer from diseases. Which combination of practices best solves this problem?

options.text: Open-field planting with flood irrigation and no pest control
Growing the tomatoes in a greenhouse with drip irrigation and controlled pest management
Sowing seeds directly in waterlogged soil without a nursery
Leaving the crop unmulched and unwatered to harden it

hoq.explanation: A greenhouse protects tomatoes from rain-borne diseases and pests, while drip irrigation supplies water efficiently and controlled management gives clean, high-quality fruit suitable for export.

hoq.questionText: After transplanting cabbage seedlings, a farmer notices many seedlings wilting in the hot afternoon sun. Which immediate management practice would best help the seedlings establish and survive?

options.text: Apply heavy nitrogen fertiliser at once to force quick growth
Uproot all wilting seedlings and discard them
Provide shade, water in the cool morning or evening, and mulch around the seedlings
Stop watering completely until the rains come

hoq.explanation: Newly transplanted seedlings lose water faster than their roots can absorb. Shading, watering during the cool parts of the day and mulching reduce moisture loss and help the seedlings recover and establish.
